claims.evidence: Retrieved text: ALT degree of rise does not reveal cause; BLT says very common to have some results not normal. 'Often not serious' is not stated and is reassuring.
claims.newSentence: Liver blood tests can point towards a possible problem but do not name the cause, and results that are not normal are very common.

claims.evidence: BLT page title: 'Liver blood tests (formerly LFT)'.
UHNM: AST is not part of the standard profile and is requested separately, so 'usually include' AST is not supported.
claims.newSentence: They can include ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.

claims.evidence: Nothing retrieved states that these tests are often routine or that abnormal results are found by chance.
UHNM: ALT inside liver cells may leak into blood when cells are damaged; ALT/AST released with liver cell damage.
Guideline text: AST is also in heart, skeletal muscle, kidney, brain and red cells so is not as liver specific as ALT.
StatPearls: most common causes of raised ALT are alcohol-induced injury, NAFLD/NASH, chronic hepatitis B or C, autoimmune hepatitis, drug or herbal-induced liver injury.
UHNM: ALP and GGT mainly linked to bile ducts; elevation may indicate a bile duct problem.
Biliary causes listed: biliary obstruction (stones, strictures, neoplasms), primary biliary cholangitis, primary sclerosing cholangitis.
A concordant GGT raises likelihood of hepatic/biliary source; normal GGT raises possibility of non-liver source such as bone.
Bilirubin pigment; high level can point to liver dysfunction or bile duct blockage. Link to jaundice is plain textbook fact.
Guideline: isolated high bilirubin most often Gilbert's syndrome; when only bilirubin is abnormal, repeat should confirm other liver tests normal.
UHNM: albumin affected only when liver disease is at a severe stage. Specific other causes (malnutrition, kidney loss, inflammation) not retrieved; only 'other factors can affect albumin'.
claims.newSentence: Albumin is affected only when liver disease is at a severe stage, and other factors can also change albumin results.

claims.evidence: Review text: enzymes are made outside the liver and rise in non-hepatic disease; patients with end-stage disease may have normal AST/ALT; BLT: normal test possible with serious liver condition.
BLT: very common to have some results not normal. 'Does not always mean a liver condition' not stated by BLT in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: The British Liver Trust says it is very common to have some liver blood test results that are not normal.

claims.evidence: BLT: possible to get a normal liver blood test with a serious liver condition. 'Liver can take a lot of damage' and 'good sign' wording was not returned.
claims.newSentence: It also says it is possible to have a normal liver blood test result and still have a serious liver condition.

claims.evidence: Search found nothing on shock, burns, pregnancy or exercise. Retrieved: drug/herbal-induced liver injury, and muscle injury, heart attack, hypothyroidism can raise ALT/AST.
claims.newSentence: Medicines and herbal supplements can raise liver enzymes, as can some non-liver problems such as muscle injury.

claims.evidence: Guidelines describe repeating tests first then further assessment if still abnormal; 'all that is needed' not stated.
claims.newSentence: Guidelines usually start by repeating the tests, and move to further checks if results stay abnormal.

claims.evidence: Reference ranges vary by laboratory; use the range on the report (BLT/hospital guidance).
NHS guidance: FIB-4 blood score used to estimate risk of scarring (fibrosis) in persistently abnormal liver blood tests.
BLT: depending on results, age and possible cause, GP may ask for more tests or regular tests. Referral wording is not BLT's.
claims.newSentence: Depending on the results, age and possible causes, a GP may arrange more tests or regular repeat tests.

claims.evidence: Persisting abnormality leads to blood tests for viral and immune causes, ultrasound for fat; medicines and alcohol reviewed.
NHS jaundice page: yellow skin/eyes can be a sign of something serious such as liver disease.
NHS: ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if skin or whites of eyes look yellow.
NHS 111 Wales: yellowing may be less noticeable on brown or black skin but the whites of the eyes look yellow.
NHS: itchy skin, darker pee and paler poo may also occur.
NHS pathway text: most common causes of abnormal liver blood tests are MASLD (fatty liver disease), alcohol and viral hepatitis.
NHS inform page was not returned. NHS hospital leaflet: best way to treat MASLD is to reverse the underlying cause; weight loss is key.
claims.newSentence: NHS hospital guidance says fatty liver disease (MASLD) is treated mainly by reversing its underlying cause, with weight loss a key part.

claims.evidence: Not stated by anything retrieved; a review search said drug options exist, so 'no specific medicine' is unverified.
Guideline: for alcohol, advise abstinence and weight loss, repeat in one month (one pathway; which one was not clear in the summary).
Retrieved: repeat liver tests after 3 months after stopping a suspect medicine; stepwise repeat first. Illness not stated.
claims.newSentence: Local guidance suggests repeating the tests, including after stopping a medicine that may be affecting the liver.

claims.evidence: If abnormality persists: further blood tests for viral and immune causes plus liver ultrasound.
Ultrasound not assessing scarring was not stated. Retrieved: FibroScan thresholds decide referral to liver clinic.
claims.newSentence: Local pathways use a FibroScan result, as well as FIB-4, to decide who is referred to a liver clinic.

claims.evidence: Search found no clear urgent-referral criteria; sentence names urgency without a route to care.
As c03: AST is not always in the standard group.
claims.newSentence: Liver blood tests, once called liver function tests, are a group of tests that can include ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.

claims.evidence: Enzymes rise in non-liver disease; normal results possible in serious liver disease (BLT).
Raised ALT/AST suggests liver cell injury; raised ALP with GGT suggests bile flow problem; normal GGT with raised ALP suggests bone.
NHS: ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if skin or whites of eyes look yellow.

additions.sentence: In alcohol-related liver injury AST is often higher than ALT, whereas in fatty liver disease ALT is often the higher of the two.
additions.evidence: AST typically higher than ALT in alcohol-related fatty liver, NAFLD shows ALT higher than AST.

additions.sentence: Muscle injury, a heart attack and an underactive thyroid can also raise ALT and AST.
additions.evidence: Non-liver sources: polymyositis, acute muscle injury, acute myocardial infarction and hypothyroidism can raise these enzymes.

additions.sentence: A normal GGT alongside a raised ALP points towards a source other than the liver, such as bone.
additions.evidence: Normal GGT raises the possibility of a nonhepatic source such as bone.

additions.sentence: Bilirubin is a pigment made when red blood cells break down, and the liver normally clears it.
additions.evidence: Bilirubin is a pigment from breakdown of red blood cells; liver normally clears it.

additions.sentence: Albumin is a protein made by the liver.
additions.evidence: Albumin is a protein the liver makes.

additions.sentence: Common causes of jaundice include alcohol-related liver disease, gallstones, hepatitis, pancreatitis and sickle cell disease.
additions.evidence: Common causes listed: alcohol-related liver disease, gallstones, hepatitis, pancreatitis, sickle cell disease.

additions.sentence: Pathways differ between areas on when to repeat tests and which scores trigger referral, so the steps a GP follows can vary.
additions.evidence: Timing varies by guideline; FIB-4 and repeat intervals differ between local pathways.

notes: Searches: 16 total across both guides (8 liver, 8 INR). Search summaries blended pages; c30 (one-month repeat after alcohol) attributed to 'one pathway' but exact pathway not identifiable. NHS inform NAFLD page and LTO page text were not returned, so those claims were reworded to what was retrieved. No numeric thresholds used.
